dedupe_keys.name: united states commuting backbone and road network deposit

description: This Figshare deposit supplies two derived U.S. commuting networks and network-metric tables. The commuter-connection backbone represents significant census-tract flows, with origin and destination tract IDs, commuter count, metropolitan-area identifier and endpoint coordinates. The backbone road network maps those selected connections onto likely driving segments and records commuter count and metropolitan context. A further CSV reports CBSA-level node and edge counts, density, clustering, modularity, reciprocity and average commuting distance; Figshare also lists line shapefiles. The accompanying GitHub page says the authors used 2017–2021 CTPP journey-to-work data, ground modes, a disparity filter at alpha 0.01 and shortest driving paths, retaining intra-CBSA links across the 50 states and District of Columbia. The repository itself is only a pointer; Figshare is the canonical data address and states CC BY 4.0 with free public access. A modeller could use the connections as regional mobility or road-demand inputs, while treating them as inferred commuting backbones, not all observed trips or a complete road inventory. The 133 MB archive, individual shapefiles and numerical construction were not downloaded or independently checked. It supports network-flow simulation and regional resilience planning, subject to the inferred-route construction.
